Crime › New Kensington

Crime in New Kensington, 2000–2024

FBI figures through 2024 · Updated Sept. 23, 2026

New Kensington Police Department · 301 11th St.

Call 724-339-7533Non-emergency, also 724-339-7534
911Emergency

Source: Westmoreland County, Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

New Kensington police reported 54 violent crimes to the FBI in 2024, or 4.6 per 1,000 residents, up from 40 (3.4 per 1,000) in 2023. That is the city's highest rate since 2019 (5.3). Property crime rose to 24.0 per 1,000 from 21.2, still lower than any year from 2001 through 2019. Police cleared 32 of the 54 violent crimes.

Source: FBI UCR via Jacob Kaplan

Violent crime since 2000

New Kensington's highest rate in the record was 10.2 per 1,000 in 2001; its lowest was 2.9 in 2020.

New Kensington

New Kensington sent no offense figures for 2000 and 2021. 2021 is missing for most Pennsylvania departments because the FBI switched to incident-based reporting that year. 2022 covers 10 months.

Aggravated assaults were 42 of the 54 violent crimes. Larceny-thefts made up 220 of the 284 property crimes. The department reported one murder or manslaughter.

How many were solved

New Kensington police cleared 32 of the 54 violent crimes they reported in 2024 and 48 of the 284 property crimes. Over its last five reporting years (2019, 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2024), the department cleared 55% of the violent crimes it reported and 21% of property crimes.

“Cleared” means the FBI counts the case as closed, usually by an arrest.

Source: FBI UCR via Jacob Kaplan

Arrests

New Kensington's most recent arrest figures sent to the FBI are for 2024: 1,670 arrests, 174 of them for drugs and 94 for driving under the influence. That is 141.1 arrests per 1,000 residents. Arrests include people who don't live in the city.

New Kensington

Source: FBI UCR via Jacob Kaplan

Officers

The FBI's 2024 staffing file lists 24 sworn officers for the New Kensington Police Department. That is 2.0 officers per 1,000 residents. Other published counts put the department at 24 full-time officers in 2023, of 27 authorized. The two counts agree. Staffing and leadership changes reported in the news are listed under police shootings, lawsuits and policy changes below.

Source: FBI UCR via Jacob Kaplan, Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

Police shootings, lawsuits and policy changes

Shootings, use of force, lawsuits, staffing, policy changes and programs reported in the news, newest first. Where the same event is also on the police blotter, it is shown once here with both sources.

Use of force. A 911 caller reported two people on bicycles trying to break into an abandoned house, and officers stopped a man and a woman in a nearby alley. Police said the man resisted handcuffing; an assisting Arnold officer used a Taser on him three times and a New Kensington officer struck him in the face several times, saying the man tried to bite him. The man was hospitalized with facial fractures and charged with aggravated assault, resisting arrest and loitering and prowling. The officer was placed on administrative leave while the DA reviewed the use of force, then resigned.

Aug. 2026 · Alley near an abandoned house, New Kensington (exact street not reported) · Source: CBS News Pittsburgh

Community program. New Kensington police introduced the newest member of the K-9 unit.

Feb. 2024 · Source: WPXI

Staffing. Council unanimously hired three full-time officers from other local agencies, bringing the roster to 24 of an authorized 27. The chief said the department had been short-staffed, with 3 to 6 officers on patrol per shift.

March 2023 · Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

Staffing. Two patrol officers resigned and a longtime detective sergeant retired, leaving New Kensington police short-staffed.

2022 · Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

Police shooting. Officers from New Kensington, Arnold and Lower Burrell found a man in his 60s walking up Center Avenue with a shotgun. New Kensington police say an officer fired after he pointed the shotgun at them, and he died at the scene. The Westmoreland County Coroner and DA investigated.

March 13, 2020 · Center Avenue near the KFC restaurant, New Kensington · Map it · Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive), Washington Post

Officer killed in the line of duty. A 25-year-old New Kensington officer, five months on the force, was shot and killed after an attempted traffic stop on Leishman Avenue when a passenger ran and fired at him during a foot chase. A suspect was arrested days later, and a Westmoreland County jury convicted him in 2019.

Nov. 17, 2017 · Leishman Avenue, New Kensington · Source: police1.com

The Washington Post's database of fatal police shootings lists one in New Kensington from 2015 through 2024, on March 13, 2020. Source: Washington Post

Incidents reported in the news

Incidents local news reported with a street location, newest first. They are a sample, not every police call.

New Kensington. Shooting. A man in his 30s was shot in the leg in the 1100 block of Fifth Avenue around 9:15 p.m. on a Tuesday and went to a hospital on his own, where he was in stable condition. The person who fired the shot fled.

July 2026 · 1100 block of 5th Avenue · Map it · Source: WPXI

New Kensington. Homicide. A man in his 40s was shot outside the New Kensington Elks Lodge on Third Avenue just before 3 a.m. following an argument inside, and he died at a hospital. Another man involved in the argument was charged with criminal homicide.

Dec. 6, 2025 · New Kensington Elks Lodge · Map it · Source: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette

New Kensington. Shooting. A man was shot twice during an argument in the courtyard of the Valley Royal Court housing complex around 12:35 p.m. and was flown to a hospital. Police said the suspect barricaded himself in an apartment and surrendered to SWAT officers without police firing any shots, and the nearby Westmoreland County Community College campus, schools and City Hall were briefly locked down.

Sept. 8, 2025 · 4th Avenue & Hileman Drive · Map it · Source: CrimeWatch

New Kensington. Police pursuit. A New Kensington officer spotted a reported stolen SUV on Tarentum Bridge Road in July 2025, and police said the driver fled at high speed to the Pittsburgh Mills mall with two passengers in the vehicle. A man was charged with kidnapping, unlawful restraint, receiving stolen property, reckless endangerment and fleeing police.

July 2025 · Tarentum Bridge Road · approximate location · Map it · Source: TribLive community news

New Kensington. Drug case. Following an undercover drug investigation, police served a search warrant at a residence in the 1200 block of Woodmont Avenue in New Kensington in April 2025 and reported seizing 27 bricks of suspected heroin or fentanyl and more than $10,000 in cash. A man was charged with several drug offenses.

April 2025 · 1200 block of Woodmont Avenue · Map it · Source: TribLive community news

New Kensington. Drug case. Agents from the state Attorney General's Office, the Westmoreland County Drug Task Force and New Kensington police served a search warrant at a home on Leishman Avenue on Nov. 18, 2024, and reported seizing nearly 600 stamp bags of suspected fentanyl, several firearms and more than $8,600 in cash. Two people were charged with drug and weapons offenses.

Nov. 18, 2024 · Leishman Avenue · approximate location · Map it · Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

New Kensington. Homicide. On July 5, 2024, a man in his 50s was found dead from stab wounds inside a home in the 600 block of Freeport Road, according to the Westmoreland County district attorney. A man was charged with criminal homicide, burglary and criminal trespass.

July 5, 2024 · 600 block of Freeport Road · Map it · Source: CrimeWatch

New Kensington. Shooting. Shortly after 7 p.m. on April 15, 2024, police said two people fired shots toward three people standing outside a building entrance at the Valley Royal Court apartment complex, near Fifth Avenue and Hileman Drive. A man was charged with three counts of attempted homicide.

April 15, 2024 · 5th Avenue & Hileman Drive · Map it · Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

New Kensington. Drug case. On Feb. 17, 2024, investigators arrested two men at a house in the 1800 block of Seventh Street and reported seizing about 22 pounds of cocaine, as part of a federal investigation into alleged cocaine trafficking. More people were later federally indicted in the case.

Feb. 17, 2024 · 1800 block of 7th Street Road · Map it · Source: TribLive community news

New Kensington. Burglary. Around 3:30 a.m. on Jan. 22, 2024, burglars drove a pickup truck stolen from another local business through the front door of a gun store on Freeport Street and took 24 firearms, according to authorities. Two men were arrested within two days and were later indicted by a federal grand jury.

Jan. 22, 2024 · Freeport Street · approximate location · Map it · Source: CBS News Pittsburgh

How these numbers are made

Crime counts come from the FBI's Uniform Crime Reporting program: the offenses each city's police department reported to the FBI, year by year, as compiled per department by Jacob Kaplan. The FBI identifies the departments by these codes: New Kensington PA06510, Arnold PA06514 and Lower Burrell PA06506.

Violent crime is murder and manslaughter, rape, robbery and aggravated assault. Property crime is burglary, larceny-theft and motor vehicle theft. Arson is listed on its own.

Rates are per 1,000 residents, using the population the FBI published for that department and year. Small towns swing from year to year; a few incidents can move a rate a lot.

Gaps: New Kensington: no offense counts for 2000, 2021; Arnold: no offense counts for 2003, 2019, 2021, 2023; Lower Burrell: no offense counts for 2021. 2021 is missing for most Pennsylvania agencies because of the FBI's switch to incident-based reporting (NIBRS).

Partial years. In some years a department reported fewer than 12 months. Those years are marked † and drawn as hollow dots, and comparisons with them use monthly averages rather than totals.

Cleared means the FBI counts the case as closed, usually by an arrest. Arrests include people who don't live in the city.

Mapped incidents are ones local news reported with a street location, checked against the original report. They are a sample, not a complete record. Locations are rounded to the hundred-block (21), an intersection (6) or a named place (2); 14 are placed on the street only and marked approximate.

Left out on purpose: names of suspects, victims and line officers (public officials such as chiefs and mayors may be named); exact house numbers; anything identifying a juvenile. Individual sexual-offense incidents are never mapped or listed; the FBI totals include them. An arrest or charge is not a conviction. The linked source articles are the original news reports and may name people; this site does not.

Policing notes: Agencies, staffing and interactions come from news reports and department pages; the two fatal police shootings are from the Washington Post's database (2015–2024). Items that could not be verified were removed.

Sources: FBI UCR via Jacob Kaplan, CBS News Pittsburgh, WPXI, Valley News Dispatch (TribLive), police1.com, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, CrimeWatch, TribLive community news, Washington Post, PennDOT crash data.
